samples.summary: The 'real engine actually honors it' test never touches production code and only round-trips a config echo
samples.evidence: preview.test.ts:631-646 calls `mermaid.initialize({startOnLoad:false, securityLevel:'strict', htmlLabels:false})` with a hardcoded literal and asserts `mermaid.mermaidAPI.getConfig().htmlLabels === false`. It does not import or invoke the code under test (`renderPass`'s initialize call in mermaid.ts:473-479), so if someone renamed, moved (e.g. to `flowchart.htmlLabels`) or deleted the key in mermaid.ts this test still passes — exactly the drift its own comment claims to guard against. It also does not pass `secure: SECURE_KEYS` or `theme`, so the config shape it exercises differs from production. Finally, `getConfig()` echoing a key it was handed does not show the engine *resolves labels* through that key; a mermaid release that kept accepting the key but stopped honouring it in label layout would leave this green while the beacon reopened. The assertion is therefore close to vacuous relative to the stated behavior (upstream honouring the root key), while being presented as the one test covering it.

samples.summary: No test covers the claim that a note cannot turn htmlLabels back on (SECURE_KEYS pinning)
samples.evidence: mermaid.ts:61-63 and 176-195 assert that `htmlLabels` is pinned in `SECURE_KEYS` "so a note cannot turn it back on", but no test asserts the `secure` list passed to `initialize()` contains `htmlLabels` (or any of the theming keys), and no test renders a fence containing `%%{init: {"htmlLabels": true} }%%` / front-matter `config: htmlLabels: true` to show it is neutralised. The new test at preview.test.ts:616-629 asserts only `objectContaining({htmlLabels:false})`, which passes even if `secure` were emptied. Grepped the whole notes package for `htmlLabels`/`SECURE_KEYS`/`secure:` (only mermaid.ts and the two new tests match) and read all mermaid cases in preview.test.ts.

samples.summary: The security behavior itself (no <foreignObject>/no fetch during layout) is asserted nowhere; only the config request is
samples.evidence: Both new htmlLabels tests assert configuration, not outcome. There is no test — in the notes vitest suite or in the browser visual/interaction lane — that renders `A[""]` with the real engine and asserts no `foreignObject`/no request. Grep for `mermaid` across *.ts/*.tsx returns only editor.test.ts, preview.ts, preview.test.ts and mermaid.ts, so the browser lane has no mermaid coverage at all. The jsdom limitation is real and acknowledged in the test comment, so this is a coverage gap to note rather than a blocker.

samples.summary: Test mutates the real mermaid global config singleton with no teardown
samples.evidence: preview.test.ts:640 calls `mermaid.initialize(...)` on the real imported module. `resetMermaidStateForTests()` (mermaid.ts:548-554) clears only this module's caches, not mermaid's own global config, so this case leaves engine-global state altered for any later case that touches the real module (e.g. the version assertion around preview.test.ts:288) — an order-dependence hazard.

samples.summary: The fixpoint loop's termination/cost claims are unverified by any test
samples.evidence: mermaid.ts:245-247 states measured costs (29 ms for a 50 kB fence, 1.5 ms for 10 kB) and unconditional termination for the new `for(;;)` loop in `stripConfigDirectives`, but the two new tests (preview.test.ts:648, 666) each exercise only two stacked carriers. No test feeds a deeply stacked or adversarial input to show the loop terminates in bounded time. Searched preview.test.ts for `stripConfigDirectives` (only referenced in a comment at line 288) and found no dedicated unit test file for mermaid.ts.
searchedFor: glob for mermaid test files (none besides preview.test.ts)

mergedFrom.evidence: preview.test.ts:640 calls `mermaid.initialize(...)` on the real imported module. `resetMermaidStateForTests()` (mermaid.ts:548-554) clears only this module's caches, not mermaid's own global config, so this case leaves engine-global state altered for any later case that touches the real module (e.g. the version assertion around preview.test.ts:288) — an order-dependence hazard.

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out verbatim. preview.test.ts:631-646 imports the real mermaid, calls mermaid.initialize({startOnLoad:false, securityLevel:'strict', htmlLabels:false}) with a hardcoded literal, and asserts mermaid.mermaidAPI.getConfig().htmlLabels === false. It never imports NotePreview or renderMermaidBlocks and never reaches the production initialize call at mermaid.ts:473-479, so it is a set-then-get round-trip through mermaid's own config store rather than a test of the engine resolving labels through the key. It also omits `secure: SECURE_KEYS` even though 'htmlLabels' is itself listed in SECURE_KEYS (mermaid.ts:192), so the config shape it exercises differs from production and a sanitizer keyed on that list would never be triggered; and it would pass unchanged if mermaid moved the key to flowchart.htmlLabels, which is precisely the drift its own comment (lines 632-638) claims to guard. I considered refuting on already-guarded: preview.test.ts:616-629 does drive the real production path (NotePreview -> preview.ts:208 renderMermaidBlocks -> mermaid.ts:473) and asserts engine.initialize was called with objectContaining({htmlLabels:false}), and preview.test.ts:287-299 pins the mermaid version to gate upstream upgrades. Those cover the mermaid.ts-side rename and the upgrade gate, so the behavior change is not entirely untested. But they do not make the flagged assertion sound — it remains an assertion that cannot fail for the behavior its comment advertises, shipped as the case that closes the upstream-honouring gap. Refuting on out-of-scope would be a judgement call against a lens that explicitly treats near-vacuous assertions as major, so under 'when in doubt, confirm' the finding stands, with low confidence given the genuine partial coverage nearby.
